thread:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a deploy service-account got bound to cluster-admin in the last rollout. I reverted the rollout but want eyes on scope and audit gaps.
aj: WTF, how did that happen? which SA?
maria: deploy-sa in namespace=infra. Someone updated the Helm chart values and the template accidentally set roleBinding.roleRef.kind: ClusterRole and name: cluster-admin.
tyler: @maria can you paste the diff?
maria: sure, pasted in gist: https://gist.redwood/example-diff and snippet: ```yaml
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: deploy-sa-binding
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deploy-sa
  namespace: infra
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
```
kevin: Oof. That explains why some deploys reached GPU pool nodes (they require node-level privileged ops).
sec-bot: Incident bot: detected privilege escalation event on deploy-sa -> cluster-admin at 1769532089. Audit events: 42.
aj: We need containment + rotate any keys the SA used. How do we find tokens in logs?
maria: tokens are short-lived. But some infra scripts exchange SA token for K8s creds. Run: `kubectl -n infra get secret -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.type=="kubernetes.io/service-account-token") | .metadata.name'` then check creation times.
tyler: Also search CI logs for `deploy-sa` usage: `rg "deploy-sa" ci/ || true`. I already flagged two workflow runs.
kevin: I'm running an audit query against our logging backend for any `exec` or `create` verbs from that subject: `resource.labels.namespace_name="infra" AND protoPayload.authentication.principalEmail:"system:serviceaccount:infra:deploy-sa"`
aj: Good. If we see any KMS unwrap calls tied to VM/agent, rotate the KMS key and revoke access. Who owns KMS key for model-checkpoints?
maria: @kevin owns the KMS key used by infra (kevin: confirm).
kevin: Confirmed. I'll start an emergency rotation and add a new key policy that denies service-account direct unwraps — require a wrapper service.
tyler: For immediate remediation: 1) remove cluster-admin binding (maria reverted rollout already), 2) create a least-priv Role with only deploy permissions, 3) rotate any long-lived creds we find, 4) run a full audit query.
aj: Agree. Also file a vuln-triage ticket for potential exposure window and include gettext of any models or data accessed.
sec-bot: Security checklist: containment done? partial. Audit pull started. KMS rotation queued. Notify compliance if PII touched.
maria: I ran a quick grep in logs for S3 access and saw two PUTs from that timeframe to backup-bucket. Might be config-only but flagging.
kevin: I'll block writes from that SA on the bucket via an IAM deny condition and check object-level writes.
tyler: Can we automate a CI lint to prevent ClusterRole binding in chart templates? Add a policy check in chart-testing: deny roleRef.kind: ClusterRole unless allowed label present.
aj: Yes, add a kubeval/opa gate. I'll open a PR after we confirm rollback stable.
maria: PR opened: https://git.redwood/pr/12345 — adds chart validation and updates chart docs.
kevin: Running post-mortem items: rotate KMS key (in progress), revoke any discovered tokens (done for old ones), add audit alert for future roleBinding.create events.
maria: Thanks all. @compliance please join if S3 artifacts include PII — tagging compliance.
sec-bot: Action items summary: [containment, rotate KMS, revoke tokens, bucket deny rule, chart lint PR, audit alert]. Assigning owners: maria, kevin, aj, tyler.
aj: I'll draft the incident note and schedule a 30m follow-up. :thumbsup:
